title: Pasta Marinara with Garlic Toast

items: 1 Tbsp kosher salt (for the pasta water)
8 slices Italian bread, ¾ inch thick
¼ cup torn fresh basil leaves

steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the 1 Tbsp salt.
Meanwhile, warm the oil and sliced garlic in a 12-inch skillet over medium-low heat 1–2 min, until the garlic sizzles and smells fragrant but hasn't browned.
Add the tomatoes, oregano, pepper flakes, ½ tsp salt and sugar. Bring to a simmer, then lower the heat and simmer 15 min, stirring now and then, until slightly thickened.
Cook the pasta until al dente, about 1 min less than the package says. Scoop out 1 cup of pasta water, then drain.

Heat the broiler with a rack 6 inches from the heat. Mix the butter and garlic powder, spread it on the bread and sprinkle with the parmesan. Broil on a rimmed sheet pan 2–3 min, until golden at the edges. Watch closely; it burns fast.
Add the pasta and ¼ cup pasta water to the sauce and toss over medium heat 1–2 min, until the sauce clings. Add more pasta water if it looks dry.
Serve topped with parmesan and basil, with the garlic toast on the side.
tips: If the sauce tastes sharp, add another pinch of sugar.
Double the sauce and freeze half for a fast weeknight dinner.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Freeze the sauce alone up to 3 months. Reheat pasta in a skillet over medium heat with a splash of water. Garlic toast is best fresh; rewarm it in a 350°F oven 3–4 min.
